NVIDIA DLSS SDK integration notes

Source:
- Official repository cloned from https://github.com/NVIDIA/DLSS.git
- Headers/link library tag used: v310.6.0
- Official release payloads audited:
  - ngx_dlss_demo_linux.zip
    sha256 da0f267ff96c55329898c29710b24a290563a23a7b7ab7941bcb4a858fc039c2
  - ngx_dlss_demo_windows.zip
    sha256 03a706be008a93341351ae8d1f0d727248db63b47d488dc69c9d2015f30af705
- Linux Super Resolution runtime pinned to v310.5.3. The v310.6.0 Linux
  `libnvidia-ngx-dlss.so` release currently fails NGX signature validation on
  native Linux drivers, so the signed v310.5.3 snippet is used until NVIDIA
  republishes a fixed v310.6.0 Linux runtime.

Bundled runtime assets:
- minecraft/resources/natives/dlss/linux/x64/libnvidia-ngx-dlss.so.310.5.3
- minecraft/resources/natives/dlss/windows/x64/nvngx_dlss.dll (DLSS SDK 310.6.0)

The NGX runtime assets are SDK `rel` Super Resolution binaries. The Linux bridge
also writes an NGX config into its app-data directory and points
`__NGX_CONF_FILE` at it so NGX has a writable models/cache path instead of
falling back to `/usr/share/nvidia/ngx`.
The generated Linux config disables the optional NGX online updater by default;
Super Resolution uses the bundled runtime/models. This avoids network requests
during synchronous discovery and first feature creation. An explicit
`__NGX_CONF_FILE` is preserved. To opt into updates with the generated config,
use `-Dminecraft.vulkan.dlss45.allowNgxUpdater=true`.
Use `-Dminecraft.vulkan.dlss45.ngxLog=verbose` to mirror NGX loader messages to
stderr while diagnosing availability failures.
Feature creation logs its duration so driver/model setup stalls can be
distinguished from later DLSS dispatches. Initial driver setup can still pause
the first DLSS frame even with online updates disabled.

DLSS uses temporal subpixel jitter by default, including at native resolution
(DLAA). The jitter supplied to NGX matches the rendered scene on the first frame
and after motion-history resets as well as during normal rendering. Disabling
it with `-Dminecraft.vulkan.dlss45.temporalJitter=false` is a diagnostic override;
repeated unjittered input can settle into distorted foliage and thin edges.
Ultra Quality uses the client's custom 1/1.3 input scale with NGX Quality mode.
The NGX UltraQuality enum is not a supported execution mode in the bundled
runtime. The bridge queries Quality's optimal creation size and validates the
custom input against its dynamic-resolution range before evaluating it.
DLSS does not use the generic fallback upscale blit by default; that path looks
like the FSR fallback and can hide that native DLSS failed. For diagnostics only,
`-Dminecraft.vulkan.dlss45.fallbackUpscaleBlit=true` restores that fallback.

Bundled link assets:
- native/dlss_bridge/lib/linux/x64/libnvsdk_ngx.a
- native/dlss_bridge/lib/windows/x64/nvsdk_ngx_s.lib

Build notes:
- Linux builds with the normal host C++ toolchain.
- Windows must be built with the MSVC ABI. NVIDIA's nvsdk_ngx_s.lib does not
  link cleanly with MinGW; use MSVC or clang-cl on Windows to produce
  resources/natives/dlss/windows/x64/dlssbridge.dll.

The DLSS bridge uses NGX Vulkan Super Resolution only. The upscaler selector
skips DLSS unless the active graphics adapter reports an NVIDIA vendor/name.
